editorial.meta_description: The HL7 FHIR Foundational Certification validates your knowledge of FHIR standards, resource structures, API behaviors, and implementation strategies.
editorial.overview: The HL7 FHIR Foundational Certification, administered by HL7 International, evaluates your proficiency in the FHIR standard. This 210-minute exam covers 5 domains and consists of 125 questions testing resource modeling, API interactions, and implementation guides. It confirms your ability to apply FHIR specifications to healthcare data exchange, ensuring you can navigate core components effectively and support interoperability across diverse clinical systems and health information technology environments.
editorial.who_should_take: This certification is for software developers, health IT analysts, and systems architects working with healthcare data. Candidates should have practical experience implementing FHIR resources and a solid understanding of healthcare interoperability standards and data exchange protocols.
editorial.preparation_strategy: Review the official FHIR specification documentation, focusing on resource definitions, datatypes, and metadata. Practice identifying resource relationships and canonical URLs. Utilize the HL7 International exam guide to understand the structure of the 125 questions. Engage with the FHIR community through official support channels to clarify implementation challenges and ensure your knowledge aligns with current standards and technical requirements.

domain_guidance.summary: This domain evaluates your ability to interpret and apply implementation guides within healthcare environments. Candidates learn to navigate canonical URLs, enforce conformance rules, and adapt FHIR profiles to fulfill custom clinical or administrative data exchange requirements.

This domain examines RESTful interaction patterns, search mechanisms, and transactional operations across FHIR servers. Candidates must understand how HTTP verbs, parameters, response codes, and resource identities govern communication between healthcare applications and services.

This domain focuses on fundamental FHIR building blocks, including resource modeling, primitive and complex datatypes, and metadata elements. Candidates demonstrate understanding of resource composition, narrative generation, extensions, and logical relationships between clinical models.

This domain addresses the practical application of FHIR resources within operational healthcare environments. Candidates must understand business identifiers, reference types, bundle construction, and strategies for mapping legacy clinical data structures into standardized FHIR representations.

This domain covers techniques for diagnosing communication errors, validating resource content against profiles, and ensuring specification compliance. Candidates learn to interpret OperationOutcome resources and resolve data formatting or structural issues effectively.

editorial.exam_day_guidance: You have 210 minutes to complete 125 questions. Manage your time carefully across the 5 domains. Read each question to identify the specific resource or API behavior being tested before selecting your answer.

faq.question_title: How many questions are on the exam?
faq.answer_text: The HL7 FHIR Foundational Certification exam consists of 125 multiple-choice questions designed to evaluate your operational knowledge of the FHIR specification across 5 distinct technical domains.

Official HL7 International documentation does not specify the exact passing percentage for this exam. Candidates are encouraged to check with HL7 International directly for the most current scoring policies and passing criteria.
Candidates are allotted 210 minutes to complete the exam. This time limit allows candidates to read each question and carefully analyze the scenarios involving FHIR resources and API behaviors.

Yes, the HL7 FHIR Foundational Certification remains an active credential offered by HL7 International. If you are seeking information regarding updated certification paths, check with HL7 International for the current certification path.
